title: REPORT on the implementation of the common foreign and security policy – 2024 annual report
part_text: 42. Welcomes the historic fall of the Assad regime in Syria; recalls that it only survived so long thanks the support of its Russian and Iranian allies and that its collapse shows they are weakened, and calls on interim authorities to break free from these alliances; welcomes the ninth Brussels Conference held on 17 March 2025, attended by Syria’s Foreign Minister, with EUR 5.8 billion pledged towards Syria’s reconstruction and humanitarian aid; reiterates its unwavering support for the people in Syria and strongly believes that stability will come from a pluralistic political transition that includes credible representatives of all components of Syrian society and of all geographical areas, that is to say all religious and ethnic communities and women, and that hinges on transitional justice and reconciliation as a path to fighting impunity; welcomes the gradual and conditional suspension of sanctions on a range of economic sectors and the indefinite extension of humanitarian exemptions, and supports a full yet reversible lifting of all sectoral sanctions while closely monitoring the political transition process; calls on the EU and its Member States to support the work of the International, Impartial and Independent Mechanism to Assist in the Investigation and Prosecution of Persons Responsible for the Most Serious Crimes under International Law Committed in the Syrian Arab Republic since March 2011; calls on the EU and its Member States to consider the establishment of a special mission, in cooperation with international partners, to help document cases of serious crimes by the Assad regime, as well as by all other factions; is deeply worried by the fragile security situation across Syria and firmly condemns the retaliatory targeting of the Alawite community; calls on the caretaker authorities to rein in all violent factions and protect all civilian citizens from violence; welcomes the landmark agreement of 10 March 2025 between Syria’s interim President and the Commander in Chief of the Syrian Democratic Forces; calls on the neighbouring countries to respect Syria’s territorial integrity and sovereignty and to immediately cease all attacks and incursions on and occupation of Syrian territory; urges the caretaker authorities to demonstrate clear commitment to the fight against terrorism and warns against the serious international security risk a sudden disengagement of the United States in the region would cause;
